newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes strongly up on weather concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes strongly up on weather concerns.

text.p: The elasticity in CBOT wheat futures was evident Monday as the market rebounded from Friday's sharply lower close to jump over one-half its daily trading limit in most contracts by Monday's closing bell.

Concerns about delays in the seeding of the U.S. spring wheat crop and talk of potential damage to portions of the U.S. winter wheat crop from this week's cold weather, were cited as key catalysts for the gains, traders said.
"The worries about flooding in the Northern Plains helped wheat," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Cold weather and snow lie at the heart of the rally.
The harshest weather was in the Northern U.S. Midwest, the key U.S. spring wheat growing region, and the activity led to concerns about delays in sowing the spring wheat crop.
"Weather Services Corp meteorologist Joel Burgio said farmers "are not going to be in the fields for weeks."
CBOT wheat closed 8-3/4 to 11-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with May up 8-3/4 at $3.80-1/2 a bushel.
The cold snap and more cold weather expected this week also led to talk that some U.S. winter wheat may be damaged.
"We are watching it, because if it gets any colder it could put some winter wheat in danger," Burgio said.
But agronomists said only minor damage, if any, occurred in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat growing region.

Wheat in Kansas may have sustained minor damage but the most vulnerable, "the southern third of the state (Kansas) dodged a bullet. Another three to five degrees and we probably could have seen some damage in that area," said Jim Shroyer, extension wheat agronomist at Kansas State University.
However, another cold snap is expected there this week, weather forecasters said.

Wheat futures rallied in CBOT's Project A overnight trend on the weather worries plus talk China bought 23,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat and talk the Philippines bought 35,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat. But there also was talk China bought up to 1.5 million tonnes of wheat from Canada, which limited gains.

USDA's weekly export inspections report was mildly bearish for wheat futures. USDA said 12.917 million bushels of wheat were inspected for export during the week ended April 3. The trade was expecting a figure from 12 million to 16 million bushels.
Technicians said first support in the May was at $3.69 and second support was at $3.64. The session low for May was $3.75-1/2.
First resistance was at $3.74 and second resistance was at $3.79. The session high for May was $3.82-1/4.
In spread trading, FIMAT Futures did five million bushels of July/May at even money and Term Commodities did 1.2 milion May/July at 1/2 to one cent, premium July, traders said.
Refco Inc bought two million bushels of July, Iowa Grain bought one million bushels of July and Cargill Inc bought one million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 22,000 contracts, below the 25,710 traded Friday.
In wheat options, Term Commodities sold 400 May $3.80 calls at 6-1/2 cents and Refco Inc bought 300 July $3.50 puts at 7-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 12,500 contracts, below the 17,831 traded Friday.
